title: Nurse or midwife registration and employment
summary: A structured route from eligibility and evidence preparation through UK professional registration and employer recruitment.
steps: Complete the NMC assessment/Test of Competence route where required
Complete health, character and registration steps
Search and apply to eligible employers
Complete the appropriate immigration route after a suitable offer
criteria: A recognised nursing or midwifery qualification, verified through the NMC
English language evidence (e.g. IELTS/OET at the NMC-required level)
The NMC Test of Competence (CBT and OSCE) if your qualification requires it
A satisfactory health and character declaration
A confirmed job offer to apply for the Health and Care Worker visa

title: Study in the UK
authority: UK institution + UK Visas and Immigration
summary: Select an institution and programme, secure admission, then complete the appropriate student immigration requirements.
steps: Prepare transcripts, references and funding evidence
Plan professional registration separately if you intend to practise
criteria: Academic transcripts meeting the programme's published entry requirements
English language evidence (usually IELTS Academic)
A personal statement and academic/professional references
A confirmed offer and CAS to apply for the Student visa

title: Internationally qualified nurse pathway
authority: Nursing Council of New Zealand + employer
summary: Review the IQN route, complete document verification and Council requirements, then use legitimate employer pathways.
steps: Meet competence, English and fitness requirements where applicable
Use Health NZ or another legitimate employer pathway
criteria: A qualification assessed as comparable by the Nursing Council of New Zealand (NCNZ)
English language evidence at the NCNZ-required level
A Competence Assessment Programme (CAP) if your qualification requires it
Satisfactory health and character checks
NCNZ registration before an employer-sponsored work visa

title: Study in New Zealand
summary: Admission and student visa steps are distinct from professional registration if you intend to practise after study.
steps: Apply for the appropriate student visa
criteria: Academic transcripts meeting the institution's entry requirements
English language evidence (IELTS Academic or equivalent)
A completed application through the institution's portal
A confirmed offer to apply for a Student visa

title: Internationally educated nurse registration pathway
summary: Canadian nursing registration is provincial/territorial. Credential assessment and regulator requirements must be checked for the chosen province.
steps: Complete regulator-specific examination or competence requirements
criteria: An National Nursing Assessment Service (NNAS) application and credential report
A pass in the relevant provincial licensing exam (commonly NCLEX-RN)
English or French language evidence depending on the province
Provincial regulatory body registration before working
An eligible immigration pathway or employer-sponsored route

title: Study in Canada
summary: Admission, study permit and future professional licensing are separate steps.
steps: Plan future registration or licensure separately
criteria: Academic transcripts meeting the programme's entry requirements
English or French language evidence
A confirmed Letter of Acceptance from a Designated Learning Institution
A study permit application after acceptance

title: Internationally qualified nurse or midwife pathway
authority: Ahpra + Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia
summary: The IQNM pathway includes assessment steps and registration standards before employment as a registered practitioner.
steps: Apply to legitimate employers and then complete immigration steps
criteria: A qualification assessed by ANMAC as comparable to an Australian standard
English language evidence (IELTS/OET at the NMBA-required level)
The NCLEX-RN or an approved bridging program if required
AHPRA/NMBA registration before working
An eligible skilled or employer-sponsored visa pathway

title: Study in Australia
authority: Australian institution + Department of Home Affairs
summary: Choose a CRICOS-registered programme and complete admission and student-visa requirements.
steps: Review Genuine Student and evidence requirements
Apply for the appropriate student visa
criteria: Academic transcripts meeting the university's entry requirements
English language evidence (IELTS Academic or equivalent)
A confirmed offer (CoE) from the institution
A Student visa (subclass 500) application after acceptance

title: Registered nurse employment and state licensure
authority: State board of nursing + relevant credentialing bodies
summary: Nursing regulation is state-based. Requirements can include credential evaluation, English evidence, NCLEX-RN and state-specific requirements.
steps: Read the state board's internationally educated nurse requirements
Complete NCLEX-RN and state licensing requirements
Use legitimate employer and immigration pathways
criteria: A CGFNS credential evaluation (and CGFNS Certification for many pathways)
A pass in the NCLEX-RN examination
English language evidence where required
A VisaScreen certificate and state board licensure
An eligible employer-sponsored visa route (e.g. H-1B or EB-3)

title: Study in the United States
summary: Admission and immigration are separate decisions; nursing practice also remains subject to state regulation.
criteria: Academic transcripts meeting the programme's entry requirements
English language evidence (TOEFL/IELTS)
A confirmed Form I-20 from the institution
An F-1 Student visa application after acceptance

title: Nurse recognition and employment in Germany
authority: Anerkennung in Deutschland (federal recognition portal) / regional health authorities
summary: A structured route from qualification recognition and German language training through to employer-sponsored work in German hospitals and care facilities.
steps: Check your profession recognition (Anerkennung) via the official portal
Prepare and submit your qualification documents for assessment
Reach the required German language level (usually B1/B2)
Complete any adaptation period or knowledge test if your qualification is only partially recognised
Search for an employer, often through licensed recruitment or direct hospital partnerships
Apply for a residence permit for qualified professionals after a job offer
criteria: A nursing/midwifery qualification eligible for the recognition (Anerkennung) process
German language evidence, typically B1 on starting and B2 within an agreed period
A completed application through the responsible regional recognition authority
A confirmed employer or recruitment partner for the work/residence permit route
links: Anerkennung in Deutschland (official recognition portal, English available)
Make it in Germany (official skilled-worker portal)
Bundesagentur für Arbeit (Federal Employment Agency job board)

title: Nursing and health-science study routes in Germany
authority: DAAD (German Academic Exchange Service) / individual universities
summary: Germany's nurse training is mostly vocational (Ausbildung) rather than university-first, alongside a smaller number of health-science and nursing-management degree programmes, some taught in English.
steps: Use the official DAAD database to find current nursing/health-science programmes and their teaching language
Confirm entry requirements for your specific route (Ausbildung vs. Bachelor programme)
Reach the required German (or English, if the programme is English-taught) language level
Apply through uni-assist or the university's own admissions portal
Apply for a student visa/residence permit after a confirmed offer
criteria: Secondary/prior academic qualification recognised as equivalent for German study
Language evidence appropriate to the teaching language of the programme
A completed application through uni-assist or the institution's official portal
A student visa application after a confirmed offer
links: uni-assist (official application portal for international students)
Make it in Germany — studying in Germany
